Annexure-A para 1.2 states verbatim: 'GREP:- Later, during the year 1997, with more natural gas availability from ONGC fields, the HVJ pipeline capacity was expanded from 18.4 MMSCMD to 33.4 MMSCMD under the Gas Rehabilitation and Expansion Project (GREP), by laying a new 36" x 505 Km pipeline from Vijaipur to Dadri (U.P.)...Upon commissioning, GREP was subsumed as a part of HVJ and a single tariff was determined for the HVJ-GREP system.' This is GAIL's own first-party regulatory account, independent of GEM, and confirms EXISTENCE via a formal regulatory filing (not marketing copy) that names this exact pipeline (GREP = P3297's own bracketed name) and gives its own Vijaipur-Dadri route. DVPL 2 & VDPL' under GAIL in its OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER section -- authorised 6,169 km / operating 6,732 km / authorised+design capacity 111.3 MMSCMD / 80.3 MMSCMD monthly supplied / 75% utilisation as of May 2026 -- confirming the whole integrated system that GREP belongs to, GREP included, is currently OPERATING (not just historically built). (3) GAIL's own live corporate website (https://www.gailonline.com/Natural_Gas.html, verified OK, contains 'GREP') lists both 'HVJ-GREP DVPL' (5,433 km) and 'DVPL-GREP Upgradation' (1,311 km) as separate, currently-operating network components 'As per PNGRB As on 30th Jun 2026'. (4) GAIL's own 2021-22 Sustainability Report Glimpses network map (https://gailebank.gail.co.in/Gailonline%20Files/Sustainability/Glimpses/GAILSustainabilityGlimpses2022.pdf, large corporate PDF, url_verifier content-check false-negative on this file too, confirmed locally via pdftotext -layout) labels both 'GREP-I' and 'GREP-II' by name on GAIL's own current (as on July 2022) network schematic, next to a 'Vijaipur - Dadri P/L' label -- an independent, GEM-unconnected confirmation that GAIL itself uses the exact 'GREP-I' name for this asset. (5) offshore-technology.com's GlobalData-sourced marketdata entry for 'Vijaipur-Dadri gas pipeline, India' (verified OK, contains 'Vijaipur' and '505') independently states: 'The 505km-long Vijaipur-Dadri gas pipeline is operated by GAIL (India)...starts at Madhya Pradesh (India) and ends in Uttar Pradesh (India)' -- confirming route and length, though see the caveat below on which of the two parallel 505km lines (GREP-I 36in vs GREP-II 48in) this generic third-party entry actually describes. PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are both correct -- GREP is unambiguously a cross-country natural-gas transmission trunk, not a gathering/process/feeder line. Owner1=GAIL (India) Ltd 100% is correct and undisputed across every source above -- GAIL is the sole named entity throughout its own regulatory filing and every third-party source. DUPLICATE check against the full 35-row India roster: P3297 (GREP-I) is NOT the same physical pipe as its closest sibling P3299 (GREP-II, roster: len=505.0 dia=48.00) despite sharing the same route, length and era-name -- GAIL's own 2018 tariff letter (Annexure-A paras 1.2 and 1.4, read directly) documents these as two historically and physically distinct construction projects laid in PARALLEL on the same right-of-way: GREP (1997, 36in x 505 km, Vijaipur-Dadri = this row, P3297) and the later 'DVPL-GREP Upgradation Phase-I' (commissioned March 2010, 'laying another 48" x 505 Km pipeline from Vijaipur to Dadri in parallel to the GREP in the same ROU' = P3299/GREP-II) -- exactly the granularity split this sweep's own scope guidance anticipated for the HVJ-GREP-DVPL family. Do not collapse P3297 into P3299 or vice versa; each is a real, separately-built pipe.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC check on StartYear1, Length, Diameter and Location. All four are directly and exactly confirmed by GAIL's own 27.11.2018 letter to the PNGRB Secretary, Annexure-A para 1.2 (read directly off the OCR'd/rendered scan, see existence finding above): 'during the year 1997...by laying a new 36" x 505 Km pipeline from Vijaipur to Dadri (U.P.)' -- this single sentence, from the pipeline owner's own first-party regulatory filing, matches GEM's StartYear1 (1997), LengthKnown (505.00 km), Diameter (36.00 in) and StartLocation/EndLocation/StartState/EndState (Vijaipur, Madhya Pradesh -> Dadri, Uttar Pradesh) with no discrepancy on any field. Vijaipur is confirmed to be in Madhya Pradesh (Guna district) and Dadri in Uttar Pradesh (Gautam Buddh Nagar district) by the same letter's own state labels ('Vijaipur to Dadri (U.P.)', with Vijaipur elsewhere in the same document located at 'Vijaipur (M.P.)') -- unlike the sibling HVJ row (P0925), where GEM's EndState/Province was found to be wrong, P3297's location fields need no correction. LENGTH is independently corroborated by a second source: offshore-technology.com's GlobalData-sourced 'Vijaipur-Dadri gas pipeline, India' entry also gives '505km-long' for a Vijaipur (M.P.) to Uttar Pradesh line. CAVEAT on DIAMETER: that same offshore-technology.com entry gives the diameter as 48 inches, not 36 -- but that figure actually matches this row's sibling P3299 (GREP-II, roster: dia=48.00), not P3297. Since both GREP-I (36in, 1997) and GREP-II (48in, 2010) run the identical 505km Vijaipur-Dadri route, this generic third-party 'Vijaipur-Dadri gas pipeline' entry appears to conflate the two parallel lines under one record and reports the newer (48in) one's diameter rather than distinguishing them -- so it does not independently corroborate P3297's own 36in figure (which rests on the single, but first-party and unambiguous, GAIL tariff letter). This is a documentation quirk in third-party literature, not a GEM error: GAIL's own account is internally consistent and explicit that GREP (1997) = 36in and the later Upgradation/GREP-II (2010) = 48in, exactly matching how GEM already has these two rows split. Flagging as a caveat for future researchers who may otherwise 'correct' P3297's diameter to 48in off a generic aggregator entry that is actually describing its sibling.

Two independent regulatory/primary sources corroborate the 107.00 figure as an accurate SYSTEM total, but as of an EARLIER snapshot: PNGRB's own historical NGPL registers (22.02.2023, 21.02.2024 and 31.03.2025 editions, all already on disk and read directly via pdftotext -layout for this sweep) list the combined 'Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur-GREP-Dahej-Vijaipur HVJ/VDPL Dadri (GREP) Upgradation DVPL2&VDPL' asset's authorised/design capacity as exactly 107.00 MMSCMD across all three editions spanning 2023-2025 -- an exact match to GEM's value, confirming 107.00 was correct for the sheet's 2023-07-13 update date. However, the CURRENT PNGRB register (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, edition MAY 2026, verified live, same document cited in the existence finding above) now lists the same combined system's authorised+design capacity as 111.3 MMSCMD -- a real ~4% increase versus 107.00, not a units slip or a different reading (authorised length is unchanged at 6,169 km across both the 2025 and 2026 editions, so this is a genuine capacity revision, not a re-scope). I am not proposing a replacement number for P3297 alone: whether Capacity should be split per segment (GREP-I's own historical ~15 MMSCMD increment) or refreshed as the current system total (111.3, spanning all five rows) is a judgment call for Update, and is a cross-row (not P3297-specific) data-convention question already flagged twice elsewhere in this same batch. Flagging as concern rather than a silent pass per the sweep's spec rule that a source must AGREE with the CURRENT GEM number, not merely mention the pipeline -- here the current regulatory reading has moved past what the sheet carries.
